explanation: I searched Mathlib (commit 83abb3e) for `IsValuativeTopology` in all its files: the only statements are the class itself, `IsValuativeTopology.of_mem_nhds_iff_vle` / `of_mem_nhds_zero_iff_vle` / `of_zero` (generic constructors from a neighbourhood basis), the basic API (`mem_nhds_iff`, `hasBasis_nhds_zero`, …), the local instance `ValuativeRel.isValuativeTopology` for the topology induced by `valuation R`, and instances for `ℚ_[p]` and `WithVal v` (`Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Valued/WithVal.lean:219`). Nothing states that the topology underlying a general `Valued R Γ₀` instance is valuative for `ValuativeRel.ofValuation hv.v`; Mathlib's file `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Valued/ValuativeRel.lean` only provides the opposite direction (a `Valued` instance from `ValuativeRel` + `IsValuativeTopology`), and `ValuativeRel.ofValuation`/`Valuation.Compatible.ofValuation` appear in Mathlib only as generic constructions. The library's own proof is not a one-step application of a single Mathlib declaration either: it needs two `letI` instance setups (for `ValuativeRel.ofValuation hv.v` and `hv.v.Compatible`) plus the bridge `Valued.mem_nhds_zero` into the `IsValuativeTopology.of_mem_nhds_zero_iff_vle` hypothesis, i.e. more than the one or two lines of routine glue, so I do not classify it as a special case of that constructor.
